title: Fireflies AI Pricing in 2026: Every Plan and Cost
summary: Fireflies AI pricing offers a free plan and paid options. See what each plan includes and costs to choose the right fit for your team.
body_markdown:
## Sending Fireflies notes into the rest of your stack with Activepieces


Copying meeting notes by hand into your CRM,[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) and task tracker is the real cost. It never shows up on an invoice, and it lands on whoever has the least time to spare.


### What Fireflies native integrations already cover


Start with what Fireflies connects to on its own. It ships integrations for common destinations like Slack, popular CRMs and task tools.


For many teams that's enough: a summary posts to a channel, a note attaches to a deal, and nobody touches anything. Check these first, because a built-in connection costs you no setup beyond signing in.


When your process has a rule in it, native integrations run out.


A built-in connection usually pushes the same thing to the same place every time. It won't read a summary, decide it concerns a support issue, and send it to a different channel than a sales call.


Whether you can reach Fireflies from outside tools at all also depends on your plan, since API access isn't offered on every tier. Confirm that on the pricing page before you plan around it.


### Route summaries and action items automatically


Think of Activepieces as an automation tool where you build a flow of steps: something happens, the flow does some work, and the result goes where you want it.


Though the flow below, titled "[HubSpot](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/hubspot) Tickets Categorization," isn't a Fireflies flow, it shows the shape you would copy.


A trigger fires on a new ticket, two AI steps rewrite and categorize the text, a Router splits the result into branches, and Slack messages go out at the bottom.


Swap the trigger for a finished meeting and you have the fix. The AI steps pull action items out of the summary, the Router sends sales follow-ups one way and internal tasks another, and the final steps post or file them.


Anything that matches no branch falls into "Otherwise," so nothing gets dropped silently.


Next, you build it once, test it on sample data, and let it run. The hand-copying stops, and so does the cost you were never billed for.
